findings.title: Preserve the light-theme color for embedded-post author links
findings.body: The light-theme branch changes the existing primary lightness adjustment from 30% to 70%, rather than preserving it while adding a dark-theme alternative. This makes embedded-post author links substantially fainter on light backgrounds; for example, a #333 primary becomes approximately #c2c2c2 instead of #707070. Keep 30% in the light branch and use the corresponding 70% secondary adjustment in the dark branch.

findings.title: Preserve group-member name contrast in light themes
findings.body: The group-member name previously used a 30% primary lightness adjustment, but the new light-theme branch uses 50%. The same unintended change occurs in mobile/user.scss at line 497. With a #333 primary and white background, this changes the name from approximately #707070 to #999999, reducing contrast from about 4.95:1 to 2.85:1. Preserve the existing 30% light-theme adjustment and add the complementary 70% secondary adjustment for dark themes.

findings.title: Retain the existing light-theme topic-map heading color
findings.body: The new light-theme branch changes topic-map h3 headings from a 20% primary lightness adjustment to 50%. This unnecessarily reduces heading contrast in light themes and gives headings the same color as the smaller h4 labels. With a #333 primary on a near-white topic-map background, the heading changes from approximately #5c5c5c to #999999. Keep the original 20% light-theme adjustment and use 80% for the dark-theme secondary branch.

findings.title: Update notification-badge text when darkening its background
findings.body: The generic notification-badge background now becomes a lightly brightened secondary color in dark themes, but its text remains the unmodified secondary color, including the explicit [href] rule. This puts dark text on a dark gray badge: with a black secondary, the new background is approximately #4d4d4d and the black text has only about 2.5:1 contrast. Previously, the primary-based background remained light and contrasted with that text. Use a contrasting dark-theme foreground, such as primary, alongside the new background.
